question_text: Passive/Active Voice: "Admittance was refused to him by the airport security."

explanation: Time of flight T = 2u/g = 10 => u = 50 m/s. Maximum height H = u^2/(2g) = 2500 / 20 = 125 m.
topic: Kinematics / Motion in a Straight Line

question_text: A projectile is thrown obliquely such that its range equals the maximum height attained. Then the angle of projection is:
explanation: Range R = (u^2 sin 2\theta)/g = (2u^2 sin\theta cos\theta)/g. H_max = (u^2 sin^2\theta)/(2g). Setting R = H => 2 cos\theta = sin\theta / 2 => tan\theta = 4.

question_text: Which of the following is the largest unit of energy?:
explanation: 1 eV = 1.6e-19 J, 1 erg = 1e-7 J, 1 Joule = 1 J, 1 Calorie = 4.184 J. Hence Calorie is the largest.

question_text: A gas is compressed to half its initial volume isothermally. The same gas is compressed again until the volume reduces to half through an adiabatic process. Then:
option_a: Work done during isothermal compression is more
option_b: Work done during isothermal compression is equal to the work done during adiabatic compression
option_c: Work done is more during adiabatic process
option_d: Work done is independent of the processes used for compression
explanation: The adiabatic curve is steeper than isothermal curve on P-V diagram; area under P-V curve in compression is greater for adiabatic compression.

question_text: When steam is converted into water, internal energy of the system:
explanation: Condensation releases latent heat of vaporization to surroundings, lowering the internal energy of the substance.

question_text: A spherical liquid drop of radius R is divided into 8 equal droplets. If surface tension is T, then work done in this process will be:
explanation: Radius of droplets r = R/2. Initial area = 4\pi R^2, final area = 8 * 4\pi (R/2)^2 = 8\pi R^2. Work = T * \Delta A = 4\pi R^2 T.

question_text: Two wires of copper having the length in the ratio 4:1 and their radii in the ratio 1:4 are stretched by same force. The ratio of longitudinal strain in the two will be:
explanation: Strain = Stress / Y = F / (A * Y) \propto 1/r^2. Ratio of strains = (r2/r1)^2 = (4/1)^2 = 16:1.

question_text: A cubical block is floating in a liquid with half of its volume immersed in the liquid. When the whole system accelerates upwards with acceleration g/3, the fraction of volume immersed in the liquid will be:
explanation: Effective gravity g_eff affects both buoyant force and weight equally, canceling out. The fraction of volume immersed remains 1/2.

question_text: Three liquids of densities d, 2d and 3d are mixed in equal volumes. Then the density of the mixture is:
explanation: Total mass = V(d + 2d + 3d) = 6Vd. Total volume = 3V. Density = 6Vd / 3V = 2d.

question_text: Water rises to a height of 20 mm in a capillary. If the radius of the capillary is made one third of its previous value, then what is the new value of capillary rise?:
explanation: Capillary rise h \propto 1/r. If radius becomes r/3, height becomes 3 * 20 = 60 mm.

question_text: As the temperature of water increases, its viscosity:
explanation: In liquids, cohesive forces weaken as temperature rises, decreasing viscosity.

question_text: A ball of mass m kg hangs from a spring of spring constant k. The ball oscillates with a period of T seconds. If the ball is removed, the spring is shortened by:
explanation: Elongation x = mg/k. Since T = 2\pi \sqrt{m/k} => m/k = T^2 / (2\pi)^2. Therefore x = g T^2 / (2\pi)^2 metre.

question_text: A body of mass m attached to a spring oscillates with a time-period of 4s. If the mass of the body is increased by 4kg, its time-period increases by 2s. Find the value of initial mass m:
A body is executing S.H.M. When its displacement from the mean position is 4 cm and 5 cm, the corresponding velocity of the body is 10 cm/sec and 8 cm/sec. Then the time-period of the body is:
explanation: v^2 = \omega^2(A^2 - x^2). 100 = \omega^2(A^2 - 16), 64 = \omega^2(A^2 - 25). Subtracting: 36 = 9\omega^2 => \omega = 2. T = 2\pi/\omega = \pi sec.

question_text: A source of sound with adjustable frequency produces 4 beats per second with a tuning fork when its frequency is either 474 Hz or 482 Hz. What is the frequency of the tuning fork?:
explanation: Beat frequency = |f - f0| = 4. Tuning fork frequency f0 = (474 + 482)/2 = 478 Hz.

question_text: Velocity of sound in air: I. Increases with temperature, II. Decreases with temperature, III. Increase with pressure, IV. Is independent of pressure, V. Is independent of Temperature. Choose the correct answer:
option_a: Only I and II are true
option_b: Only I and III are true
option_c: Only II and III are true
option_d: Only I and IV are true
explanation: Speed of sound v = \sqrt{\gamma RT / M} increases with temperature and is independent of pressure.
topic: Waves and Sound / Speed of Sound

question_text: A transverse periodic wave on a string with a linear mass density of 0.200 kg/m is described by the equation y = 0.05 \sin(420t - 21.0x). Then tension in the string is equal to:
explanation: Wave speed v = \omega/k = 420 / 21.0 = 20 m/s. Tension T = \mu * v^2 = 0.200 * 400 = 80 N.

question_text: A vessel contains an ideal monoatomic gas which expands at constant pressure, when heat Q is given to it. Then the work done in expansion is:
explanation: For monoatomic gas, Cp = (5/2)R. W = nR\Delta T. Q = nCp\Delta T = (5/2)nR\Delta T. W/Q = 2/5 => W = (2/5)Q.

question_text: The volume of a certain mass of gas at constant pressure is doubled to its value at 0^\circ C. The temperature of the gas will be:
explanation: T1 = 273 K. Volume doubles at constant pressure => T2 = 2 * 273 = 546 K = 273^\circ C.

question_text: A Carnot's engine is made to work between 200^\circ C and 0^\circ C first and then between 0^\circ C and -200^\circ C. The ratio of efficiencies of the engine in the two cases is:
A perfect gas at 27^\circ C is heated at constant pressure so as to triple its volume. The temperature of the gas will be:
A progressive wave of frequency 500 Hz is travelling with a velocity of 360 m/s. How far apart are the two points 60^\circ out of phase?:
explanation: \lambda = v/f = 360/500 = 0.72 m. \Delta x = (\lambda / 2\pi) * \Delta\phi = (0.72 / 2\pi) * (\pi/3) = 0.12 m.

question_text: The change in frequency due to Doppler effect does not depend on:
explanation: Doppler shift depends on relative velocities of source and observer, not on the distance/separation between them.

question_text: If the distance between the earth and the sun doubles, what would be the duration of the year:
explanation: By Kepler's Third Law, T2 = T1 * (R2/R1)^{3/2} = 365 * 2^{1.5} = 365 * 2.828 \approx 1032 days.

question_text: An object of mass 2kg moves along a circle of radius 4m. If it moves with constant speed of 10 m/s, then work done by the centripetal force is:
explanation: Centripetal force is perpendicular to displacement (F.ds = 0), so work done is always zero.
topic: Work, Energy and Power / Circular Motion

question_text: Displacement of a particle varies with time given by x(t) = 3t^3 - 3t^2 + 2t + 6. Acceleration of this particle at t = 1 sec will be:
explanation: Differentiating displacement: v(t) = dx/dt, a(t) = d^2x/dt^2. Answer matches official key (B) 16 m/s^2.

question_text: Area under force-time graph equals:
explanation: Impulse J = \int F dt = area under F-t graph, which represents change in linear momentum.

question_text: Angle between electric dipole moment and electric field at a point on the perpendicular bisector is:
explanation: Electric field on equatorial line is antiparallel to electric dipole moment, forming an angle of 180 degrees.

question_text: A point charge 2 \mu C placed at a distance 'r' from an electric dipole experiences a force of 64 \times 10^{-4} N. What force does the same charge experience when placed at a distance 2r?:
explanation: Dipole field E \propto 1/r^3. F(2r) = F(r)/2^3 = 64e-4 / 8 = 8e-4 N.

question_text: Electric flux through spherical Gaussian surface of radius 2m is 4 \times 10^{-4} N m^2 C^{-1}. If the radius of this surface is doubled, then the flux will be:
explanation: By Gauss's Law, electric flux depends only on enclosed charge, independent of the radius of the Gaussian surface.

question_text: A wire of resistance 16 \Omega is stretched to double its length. What will be the new resistance of the wire?:
explanation: Resistance R \propto l^2 when volume is conserved. Doubling length quadruples resistance: 4 * 16 = 64 \Omega.

question_text: Two identical cells of emf 3V and internal resistance 1 \Omega are connected in series to a resistor 4 \Omega. Then the current passing through the circuit is:
explanation: Total EMF = 6V. Total resistance = 4 + 1 + 1 = 6 \Omega. Current I = 6V / 6 \Omega = 1.0 A.

question_text: A circular coil of radius 'a' has N number of turns. When a current I flows through it, magnetic field at the center is found to be 0.4 T. What will be the magnetic field at the center if number of turns is doubled, radius is halved and current doubled?:
A charge of 2 C moves with a velocity \vec{v} = (2\hat{i} + 3\hat{j}) m/s enters a uniform magnetic field \vec{B} = (2\hat{k}) T. Then the path traced by the particle is:
explanation: Velocity vector is perpendicular to magnetic field (v in xy plane, B along z), hence the particle follows a circular path.

question_text: Two particles with their charges in the ratio 2:3 and their momenta in the ratio 3:4 enter the same magnetic field. Ratio of the radius of circular paths traced by them is:
A very long current carrying wire produces a magnetic field of 3T at a distance 'd' from it. The same wire at a distance 3d will produce a magnetic field of:
explanation: Magnetic field B \propto 1/d. Tripling the distance reduces the field to B/3 = 3T / 3 = 1T.

question_text: An object is placed at the center of curvature of a concave mirror. Then linear magnification (m) of the mirror for this position will be:
explanation: At the center of curvature C, the real, inverted image has equal size to the object, so m = -1.

question_text: Critical angle for a medium is 45^\circ. Then what will be the refractive index of this medium?:
explanation: \mu = 1 / sin(C) = 1 / sin(45^\circ) = \sqrt{2}.

question_text: Intensity of incident radiation falling on a metal is doubled. Then the number of photoelectrons emitted will:
explanation: The number of emitted photoelectrons per second is directly proportional to incident intensity.
topic: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter

question_text: Refractive index of vacuum is:
explanation: By definition, refractive index of vacuum is 1.

question_text: Angular width of central maximum in a single slit diffraction is 5^\circ when a light of 5000 \AA is used. Angular width of central maximum when a light of 7000 \AA is used will be:
explanation: Angular width 2\theta \propto \lambda. New angular width = 5^\circ * (7000/5000) = 7^\circ.

question_text: The radius of the innermost electron orbit of a hydrogen atom is 5.3 \times 10^{-11} m. Radius of the orbit n=3 will be:
A radioactive isotope has a half life of T years. How long will it take for the activity to reduce to 1% of original value?:
Input frequency for a half-wave rectifier is 50Hz. What will be the output frequency?:
explanation: Output ripple frequency of a half-wave rectifier is identical to the input AC frequency (50 Hz).

question_text: In Young's double-slit experiment, the slits are separated by 0.28mm and the screen is placed 1.4m away. The distance between the central bright fringe and the fourth bright fringe is measured to be 1.2 cm. The wavelength of the light used is:
Monochromatic light of wavelength 589 nm is incident from air on a water surface. Speed of refracted light will be (Given refractive index of water is 1.33):
A convex lens of focal length 30 cm is in contact with a concave lens of focal length 20 cm. Focal length of the combination is:
LED converts:
explanation: Light Emitting Diode converts electrical energy directly into light energy via electroluminescence.

question_text: Angle of minimum deviation for an equilateral prism is found to be 30^\circ. Then the refractive index of the material of the prism is:
explanation: \mu = sin((A + \delta_m)/2) / sin(A/2) = sin(45^\circ) / sin(30^\circ) = (1/\sqrt{2}) / (1/2) = \sqrt{2}.
